clue.text: Having less hair to tear? Nonsense

parts.note: balder means having less hair on the head
to tear is to rush or dash about

explanation.surface: A balding man is tempted to tear out what hair he has left, then dismisses the idea as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk or writing, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Road surfacing while parking has to stop

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as he spoke'
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
halt means stop

explanation.surface: A warning that roadworks force parking to cease.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry material laid on top of roads to make their surface.

clue.text: Record is set in Washington

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so is goes within the letters for Washington

parts.note: DC, District of Columbia, stands for Washington

explanation.surface: A record album is said to take place in the American capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or similar recording medium.

clue.text: Go after concerning journey home?

indicators.note: after puts the word for go behind the word for concerning

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to set off once a matter has been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a loose description rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A return is the trip back to where you started, so a journey home is one example.

clue.text: Boil tuna after mincing and washing

indicators.note: mincing chops something up, so the letters of boil tuna are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: boil the tuna once it has been minced, then wash up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablution is a formal word for the act of washing oneself.

clue.text: Individual and unpleasant smell on article

indicators.note: on places the smell word before the article in a down answer

parts.note: a hum is British slang for a bad smell
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A person and a nasty whiff are found on a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a hum is a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A human is an individual person, a single member of mankind.

clue.text: It's sweeter when in difficulties knowing how to handle oneself

indicators.note: letters in difficulties are in trouble, thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that life is better in hard times for someone savvy.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetwise describes someone with the shrewd practical sense to cope in tough urban life.

clue.text: Sorts English font finally, to prepare for printing

parts.note: types means sorts or kinds

indicators.note: finally selects only the closing letter of font

parts.note: last letter of font

explanation.surface: A printer sorts English fonts to get a page ready for the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Sorts and font both sound like printing jargon, which fits the surface but here sorts just means kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: To typeset is to arrange type or text so that it is ready to be printed.

clue.text: Offer to pay for newcomer in the US

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as with a payment
to foot a bill is to pay for it

explanation.surface: Someone proposes to cover the cost for a new arrival in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderfoot is American slang for a novice or someone new to a rough outdoor life.

clue.text: I'm trapped by burning ceiling

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside, so I'm goes inside the word for burning

parts.note: lit means burning, alight
taken as its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone stuck under a ceiling that is on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceiling in the figurative sense is an upper limit, as on prices.

clue.text: Looking good in some fine attire

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone looks smart dressed in elegant clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat describes a tidy, smart appearance, which is looking good.

clue.text: Show in reconstructed PE centre

indicators.note: reconstructed means built again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A display staged in a rebuilt physical education centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretence is a false show, an outward display that is not genuine.

clue.text: Synthetic rubber rope found coiled in river at Northampton

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the river's name

parts.note: the Nene is the river flowing through Northampton

indicators.note: a coiled rope is twisted around, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A synthetic rope is discovered wound up in an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nene is a river in the English Midlands that runs through Northampton.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoprene is a man-made polymer used like rubber, as in wetsuits.

clue.text: Set a high value on European encounters after returning

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters are read backwards
after puts the European letter behind the word for encounters

parts.note: meets means encounters

explanation.surface: A European values the people met on the way home.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something is to regard it highly, to respect and value it.

clue.text: Struggle of doctor getting into his white garment?

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the doctor letters go inside the garment

parts.note: a doctor wears a white coat
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor struggles to put on his white coat.
explanation.walkthrough: His refers back to the doctor, whose garment is the white coat; the question mark admits that is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat means a fight or struggle between opposing forces.

clue.text: Cover wager about large bank losing billions

indicators.note: about means around, so the wager goes around the other letters

parts.note: a bet is a wager
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: losing means the letter for billions is dropped from bank

parts.note: the word itself

explanation.surface: A financial story: a bet on a big bank that has lost billions.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket is a bed covering, and to blanket is to cover completely.

clue.text: Bring to light contents of cell — lice and nits?

indicators.note: contents of means the inside letters, so each word loses its first and last letter

parts.note: middle letters of cell
middle letters of lice
middle letters of nits

explanation.surface: An inspector finds a cell crawling with lice and their eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or evoke information, bringing it out into the open.

clue.text: What could be keeping up standards?

definitions.text: What could be keeping up standards?

parts.words: What could be keeping up standards?
parts.note: standards here are flags, and the thing holding them aloft is the pole they fly from

explanation.walkthrough: Keeping up standards sounds like maintaining quality, but a standard is also a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagpole is the tall staff on which a flag or banner is raised.

clue.text: A climber perhaps ascended

parts.note: a rose is an example of a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A mountaineer, perhaps, went up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, meaning went up or got up.

clue.text: Dress I am returning with wrong mark in it

indicators.note: in it means the mark goes inside the turned-round letters
returning means I am is read backwards

parts.note: taken as its letters
an X is the mark used to show an answer is wrong

explanation.surface: Someone coming back with a dress that has a mistake in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long skirt or dress reaching to the ankles.

clue.text: Noise made by cat's pursuer girl's seen off

indicators.note: seen off means sent away, so the girl's name is removed from pursuer

parts.note: the word itself
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The cat's chaser is driven off by a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A purr is the low continuous vibrating sound a contented cat makes.

clue.text: Strange ooze absorbing nitrogen gas

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the rearranged letters surround the nitrogen symbol
strange means odd or out of order, so the letters of ooze are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: An odd slime soaks up nitrogen, a chemistry curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, a gas in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Laugh seeing the French on pitch

indicators.note: on places the French article after the throw word

parts.note: to chuck is to pitch or throw
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone laughs to see French players on a pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks like a sports field, but here it is the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A chuckle is a quiet laugh.

clue.text: Preferred to make a speech for those voting

parts.note: elect, as in the president-elect, means chosen or preferred
to orate is to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: A candidate chose to address the voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote in an election.
